comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
In direction (a)⇒(b), after deleting border prototype $p$ (opposite-label neighbor $p'$) and perturbing to $x_\eta=w+\eta u\in R_p$, the proof asserts $h_S(x_\eta)\ne y_p$ on a positive-measure set.

**Gap.** If $p'\notin I_S$, then $\nu_S(x_\eta)$ is the nearest REMAINING $S$-prototype, which could be a FARTHER same-label ($y_p$) point — giving $h_S(x_\eta)=y_p=h_T(x_\eta)$ and NO disagreement at $x_\eta$. The step 'the only label-$y_p$ prototype within distance $\|w-x_{p'}\|+O(\eta)$ is $x_p$' excludes CLOSER same-label points but not a farther same-label $S$-point becoming nearest after $x_p$ is deleted. Hence existence of a positive-measure disagreement set is unproven.

**Fix.** Add an explicit lemma: on a positive-measure strip of $R_p$ adjacent to relint $F=\overline{R_p}\cap\overline{R_{p'}}$, the nearest $S$-point must carry the opposite label (use that $p'$ is the unique second-nearest and analyse the strip toward $F$). This is the most delicate gap in the necessity direction.
